title: 1.5 Million Impacted by Data Breach at South Korean Electric Company KEPCO
content_md: South Korean state-owned electric company Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO, KRX: 015760, NYSE: KEP) has disclosed a data breach impacting approximately 1.5 million people. The incident, the company says , involved KEPCO ON, its integrated customer service portal, and the supplier relationship management (SRM) platform, which handles procurement and service contracts. KEPCO attributed the incident to an external attacker and noted the growing sophistication of AI-driven cyberattacks. It did not disclose how the attacker gained access or confirm that AI was used in this breach. According to KEPCO, it suspended the affected services immediately after discovering the incident, blocked external access, conducted a thorough review of the relevant systems, and took remediation actions. On November 20, the company confirmed that data was exfiltrated from its systems, including electricity customer and SRM user information. From KEPCO ON, the hackers stole the personal information of 650,487 people, including names, addresses, phone numbers, unique ID numbers, customer numbers, card numbers and details, bank names, bank account numbers, account-holder names, card issuers, cardholder names, and billing/payment details.
